headline: Weekly Your Wellbeing check-in survey launched for staff and researchers
detail: Reported to the Crisis Leadership Team and to faculty level, and designed partly to test whether crisis measures were harming under-represented staff.
quote: The UCL Your Wellbeing check-in survey launches today. This short, weekly survey is the way to check in with you regularly to find out how you are coping with the coronavirus crisis and the immense amount of change that it has caused.
notes: A weekly internal measurement running alongside, and four months before, the published case statistics. The survey results are not in the archive; only the fact of their collection is.

headline: Wellbeing survey results reviewed weekly by the Provost and Crisis Leadership Team
quote: The Provost and Crisis Leadership Team review these results in person every week. They form a central part of their decision-making process
notes: Establishes that a weekly internal data feed was already part of decision-making before the case statistics existed. Relevant to how the October 2020 case page was used.

headline: Connected Learning Essentials staff development course launched
detail: Over 800 colleagues had engaged with it within nine days.
quote: Connected Learning Essentials, UCL’s staff development course, is designed to help colleagues with the move to online and socially distant teaching. More than 800 colleagues have engaged with the course since it launched on Monday 15 June.
notes: Filed on 15 June, the launch date; reported in issue 72 of 24 June.

headline: Fieldwork permitted to restart under Dean-approved risk assessment
detail: Conditional on voluntary participation, the reopening plans, and UK and destination travel rules. International travel on UCL business remained barred until 1 August.
quote: Fieldwork can restart from this week, as long as individuals wish to take part

headline: Virus Watch launched with 42,500 participants
detail: Regular symptom surveys, a movement-tracking app, and blood tests and swabs for 10,000 participants, intended to inform government and NHS planning.
quote: This week UCL launched Virus Watch, one of the largest and most comprehensive studies of COVID-19 in the UK, with 42,500 people taking part to help us learn more about the next phase of the pandemic.
notes: UCL running national community surveillance while having no case data of its own. Its own counting begins 12 October 2020.

headline: UCL passes £1m raised for its pandemic response
detail: Directed at research on tracking, treating and preventing the virus, at societal recovery, and at student hardship.
quote: UCL has raised over £1m to drive the university’s response to the pandemic, through generous donations from our supporters, alumni and friends.

headline: Undergraduate bursaries increased for 2020-21
detail: The lowest income band rose from £2,500 to £3,350, with uplifts across all four bands, applied automatically and extended to students who joined from 2017-18.
quote: UCL is increasing the amount of financial support available as part of our Undergraduate Bursary for the academic year 2020/21.
notes: Categorised accommodation as the nearest available slot for student financial support; the category list has no hardship or finance value.

headline: Staff allowed onto campus by rota to collect belongings
detail: Buildings opened on set dates in morning or afternoon slots, by request through Faculty Directors of Operations or Security.
quote: From tomorrow, Wednesday 1 July, it will be possible to collect personal belongings from campus on a pre-arranged, rota basis.
notes: Filed on 1 July, the effective date; announced 30 June.

headline: Taught postgraduates given access to Student Centre and Click and Collect
detail: For students unable to study remotely, by advance booking, with distancing and face coverings in force.
quote: From Monday 6 July taught postgraduate students who are unable to study remotely may use the pilot Student Centre learning spaces and the Click & Collect service for the Main and Science Libraries
notes: The first return of any students to campus since March, and it is limited to those who cannot work at home.

headline: UCL signs the London Higher COVID-19 Secure Charter
detail: Ten principles for a safe return to campus, adopted by more than twenty London institutions.
quote: London Higher has today published their COVID-19 Secure Charter. The charter sets out ten key principles that member institutions are working on to ensure a safe return to campus for students across London this autumn.
notes: A sector-level commitment with a named document. London Higher is a stage 2 retrieval target for the sector track.

headline: Roadmap for returning to campus published, targeting 25% of staff on site
detail: Setting out which buildings would reopen and when, while most staff continued to work from home.
quote: we are also beginning to work towards a return to something approaching normality, with the launch today of our roadmap for returning to campus . This sets out the plan and supporting guidance for reopening buildings gradually and safely, so that around 25% of staff can be back on site at any one time.
notes: The 25% ceiling is the planning assumption behind the autumn 2020 campus population, and therefore behind the on-campus case counts when they begin in October.

headline: UCL keeps 2 metre distancing after the government moves to one metre plus
detail: Justified by reference to the Chief Medical Officer's advice and PHE guidance, and by the need for flexibility if guidance changed or a second wave came.
quote: although the government has announced its “1 metre plus” approach to social distancing, we have confirmed that we will continue to use a 2 metre guideline for timetable planning for Term 1
notes: The clearest deliberate divergence from national policy in the record, and in the cautious direction. It set the room capacities for the whole of Term 1 and so directly shaped how many people were on campus in autumn 2020.

headline: UCL cites the Leicester local lockdown as a reason for caution
quote: The local lockdown announced in Leicester last week, and the possibility of lockdowns in some London boroughs, show us that we cannot yet take our safety for granted.
notes: An explicit reference to a national event shaping a UCL decision. The Leicester lockdown of 29 June 2020 is a stage 2 retrieval target.

headline: Temperature checks extended from the Student Centre across campus
detail: Alongside handwashing, distancing, additional cleaning, face coverings and PPE where appropriate.
quote: trialling temperature checks at the Student Centre, which we’re now rolling out across campus
notes: Temperature screening was later widely judged ineffective for COVID-19. Recorded as what UCL did, not as a measure that worked.

headline: Four additional closure days added, extending the Christmas break to two weeks
detail: Friday 28 August before the bank holiday, and 21 to 23 December, closing UCL from 18 December 2020 to 4 January 2021.
quote: UCL will be closed from 5:30pm on Friday 18 December 2020 until 9am on Monday 4 January 2021.
notes: Decided in July. The closure period turned out to coincide with the Alpha wave and the second national lockdown, and with the highest weekly case count in the whole UCL series.

headline: Digital first recommended for Term 1, with local teams deciding specifics
detail: A mix of asynchronous and synchronous learning with some campus-based, laboratory and studio teaching, and decisions devolved to programme teams.
quote: In Term 1, UCL recommends a ‘digital first’ approach (a mixture of asynchronous and synchronous learning), with some campus-based face-to-face as well as lab- and studio/practice-based teaching activity for students, led by academic or teaching staff.
notes: Names Tier 4 visa requirements and the implications of wholly online programmes as planning considerations, which is an immigration constraint on teaching mode.

headline: UCL joins the Hidden Disabilities Sunflower scheme
detail: So that staff with non-visible disabilities could signal a need for help while returning to campus.
quote: UCL has recently signed up to the Hidden Disabilities Sunflower scheme , which allows colleagues to discreetly signal to others that they may need additional help

headline: Government research support package announced in two parts
detail: A COVID-19 Grant Extension Allocation to sustain UKRI and National Academies awards to September 2021, and a Research Stabilisation Package of low-interest loans with some grants.
quote: At the end of last month, the UK Government announced a support package for research, made up of two elements.
notes: Dated to June 2020 with month precision, because the newsletter says only 'at the end of last month'. Day precision would assert more than the source supports. The primary announcement is a stage 2 retrieval target and the row should be re-dated to day precision once it is found.
